newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to cut reserve ratio by 1.5-2.0 pts in Q1.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to cut reserve ratio by 1.5-2.0 pts in Q1.

text.p: South Korea will cut the bank reserve ratio by 1.5 to 2.0 points from the current 5.5 percent during the first quarter of this year as part of financial reforms, the central Bank of Korea said on Thursday.
"The reserve ratio cut will help lower interest rates," said Min Sung-ki, deputy director at the bank's monetary planning division. He said the ratio would be cut at the earliest possible date.
In November, the central bank cut the reserve ratio to an average 5.5 percent from 7.4 percent.
President Kim Young-sam said in January a committee for financial reform would be established to draw up proposals aimed at improving competitiveness.
The bank said ceilings for the issue of certificates of deposit (CDs) would be abolished in the first quarter of 1997.
Currently, CD issues are limited to 150 percent of shareholders' equity for commercial banks and 400 percent for specialised banks.
But banks must set aside funds equivalent to two percent of CD issues as a reserve to prevent too abrupt shifts of funds to CDs. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5645
